diagnosis: The learner is stuck on a single module (Module 4 — Pandas GroupBy in TVTC-DS1) with three assessment attempts and scores trending downward: 48 → 44 → 41. This is not a motivation problem — it is a prerequisite gap: Python fundamentals and functional programming concepts (iteration, data structures) likely need reinforcement before Pandas GroupBy is approachable. Separately, DRB-204 Applied Statistics was dropped after only 4 of 30 expected hours, suggesting either wrong modality or an intimidating entry point. In contrast, the learner shows clear strength in adjacent tools: Advanced SQL completed fast with 96%, Power BI completed with 92% — both below expected hours — signalling high ability when the foundation is solid.

alternative_paths.name: Python Foundations First, Then Re-enter TVTC-DS1
alternative_paths.approach: Pause TVTC-DS1. Complete a short Python fundamentals module covering loops, list comprehensions, dictionaries, and functions before returning to the Pandas GroupBy module. This is a prerequisite fix, not a course replacement.
alternative_paths.why_this_fits: Declining scores across three attempts on the same module strongly indicate a missing foundation rather than inability. Shoring up core Python syntax will make GroupBy logic learnable rather than abstract.
alternative_paths.first_step: Identify and complete a standalone Python basics resource (covering data structures, loops, and functions) — aim for 10–15 hours — then reattempt Module 4 of TVTC-DS1.

alternative_paths.name: Project-Based Python Learning via a Real Dataset
alternative_paths.approach: Instead of continuing the structured course, work through a self-directed data project using a public dataset (e.g., a Saudi open-data source). Apply GroupBy and aggregation to answer a real business question, using documentation and community forums as the primary support mechanism.
alternative_paths.why_this_fits: The learner has verified SQL and Excel skills and completed two courses efficiently — they learn well when context is concrete. A hands-on project may unlock Pandas concepts that abstract assessments have not.
alternative_paths.first_step: Choose one dataset from data.gov.sa, define three analytical questions answerable with GroupBy, and build a Jupyter notebook to answer them — committing to a small deliverable before the next assessment attempt.

alternative_paths.name: Statistics via Applied Power BI Path
alternative_paths.approach: Replace DRB-204 (which was dropped early) with a statistics track embedded inside Power BI — learning descriptive statistics, distributions, and aggregation through DAX measures and visual analytics rather than abstract classroom instruction.
alternative_paths.why_this_fits: The learner scored 92% in Power BI and is clearly comfortable in that environment. Learning statistics through a tool they already succeed in changes the modality from lecture-heavy to applied, addressing the likely reason DRB-204 was dropped.
alternative_paths.first_step: Search for a Power BI + DAX statistics-focused practice set and build a dashboard that includes mean, median, variance, and trend analysis on a chosen dataset — treating each measure as a statistics lesson.

recommended_adjustments: Do not attempt Module 4 of TVTC-DS1 a fourth time without first addressing Python fundamentals — a fourth attempt with the same preparation will likely yield the same or lower result.
Formally pause DRB-204 rather than leaving it abandoned; revisit it only after Python progress is restored and through an applied or tool-integrated modality.

Leverage existing SQL strength immediately: build a portfolio project that combines Advanced SQL and Power BI to produce a data analysis report — this creates a visible credential while Python is being reinforced.

Set a concrete checkpoint: if the TVTC-DS1 Module 4 assessment score does not exceed 60% after completing a Python foundations refresher, escalate to a peer-study group or mentored session focused specifically on GroupBy and aggregation logic.
motivation_note: Your 96% in Advanced SQL and 92% in Power BI make it clear you can master technical material — the Python wall you have hit is a very common prerequisite gap, not a signal about your potential. Addressing the foundation now will make the Pandas module click, and you will move faster for having done it properly.
